title: Reconstruction error from a digitized Kaplan-Meier curve was too small to change which method ranks best for RMST
question: When the comparator arm must be reconstructed from a published Kaplan-Meier figure, does the reconstruction error change which method performs best, as it would if it penalized likelihood-based methods more, or does it only shift every method's error?
design: OUT-13's publication and reconstruction model; Kaplan-Meier and Weibull RMST on true and reconstructed data and the digitized curve integrated directly; fine or coarse figures, 6-monthly risk table or none, spread or clustered censoring. 8 cells, 1000 replicates each.
answer: Yes, for RMST within follow-up the omission is harmless. Reconstructing the comparator arm from a pixel-rounded Kaplan-Meier figure changed neither the ranking of Kaplan-Meier and Weibull RMST (same in all 8 cells) nor any method's RMSE by more than 1%: it added 0.003 to 0.040 months of bias to Kaplan-Meier RMST and 0.006 to 0.059 to Weibull RMST against a sampling SD of about 0.5 months. The likelihood-based method was more exposed, as predicted, but immaterially.
findings: Share of mean squared error attributable to reconstruction: -0.6% to 0.1% (KM), -0.4% to 0.9% (Weibull), zero within Monte Carlo error.
Reconstruction bias was upward and largest at coarse resolution, from reading drops at pixel-column centers.
Integrating the digitized curve directly performed as well as reconstruction.
not_answered: Reconstruction error only; RMST within follow-up only (extrapolated survival and hazard ratios not ranked); no human digitization variability; other access mechanisms not simulated. Peer review has not been done.
